one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-01 to the 2026-10-30 close (Oct 31 is a Saturday). Q3 2026 results are probably inside it: 2026 reporting has run about two weeks earlier than 2025 (Q2 on Jul 29 vs Aug 13) and aggregators list Oct 28; Hudbay usually issues the call notice ~3 weeks ahead and none was found as of Oct 2, which is normal (src 20). I put ~65% on an in-window print. The bar is high (consensus $0.36-0.37 vs Q2 actual $0.28, src 17): copper in Q3 was flat to up vs Q2, but gold fell from ~$4,450 (Aug 31) to ~$4,157 (Sep 30) on Kalshi settlements (src 9), while delayed Peru concentrate shipped in July helps volumes. Net I see no clear surprise direction, so the event mainly widens the distribution. The Sep 28 Snow Lake upgrade (src 16) and the early Oct-2 print near $27.20 (thin volume) are a small positive, offset by copper slipping to $6.58 on Oct 2 (src 7); the thin Kalshi Oct-30 copper book is treated as weak evidence only. No Peru corridor blockade affecting Constancia turned up in October 2026 searches (the Sep 2025 shutdown is the precedent risk, src 18, 19). Median ~$26.3 (a hair above spot), monthly vol ~18.5% with a 15% fat-tail component (28%) for the earnings print.

fair_value.method: Blend of 2027E EV/EBITDA (7.0x on $1.55B less ~$20M attributable net debt = $24.4, 40%), SOTP (operations 6x $1.55B + Copper World 70% $1.55B + Cactus $0.91B - $0.02B = $26.4, 40%) and P/E (17x $1.55 2027E EPS = $26.4, 20%) on 444.1M shares -> ~$25.6.

methods.inputs: 2027E EBITDA $1.55B x 7.0x = EV $10.85B; less attributable net debt $0.02B; / 444.1M shares = $24.4

Current EV ~ $11.6B (444.1M x $26.18, src 14, plus ~$20M net debt, src 15) is ~9.2x TTM $1.27B and ~7.5x my 2027E; 6-8x forward is the usual band for mid-tier copper producers at near-record prices; 7x mid-point because growth projects are valued separately in the SOTP.

PFS NPV8 $1.1B at $3.75/lb and $1.7B at $4.25/lb, i.e. +$0.6B per +$0.50/lb (src 3); at a ~$5/lb long-term deck ~$2.6B, less capex inflation flagged above the PFS (src 15) -> ~$2.2B, x70% = ~$1.55B, ~ x0.85 pre-sanction risk plus Hudbay's 70% of $334.5M ring-fenced cash. Cross-check: Mitsubishi's $600M for 30% implies ~$1.4B for 70% (src 5).
Shares issued worth $1,135.6M (note 4, src 14; the C$1.48B headline in src 4 was Canadian dollars), ~20% haircut as a PFS-stage project.

Q3 2026 consensus $0.37 (9 analysts, src 17) annualizes to ~$1.48 on 444M shares; Q2 actual $0.28 beat $0.25 (src 1, 17). The +28% guided copper volume step-up (src 3) is partly offset by lower Constancia gold, higher depreciation and a slightly lower gold price, so ~+5% -> ~$1.55.

Cut from 20x in round 1 because the EPS base is now higher (consensus at near-record metals): high-teens is a fair forward multiple for a growing copper producer at peak-ish prices. The community 25.5x narrative (src 11) is treated only as a bullish ceiling, not an input to the number.

bear.story: Copper unwinds toward ~$5/lb on demand or tariff-driven destocking and gold slips further; the Copper World DFS shows a large capex jump or sanction slips into 2027; Copper Mountain ramp disappoints so 2027 copper lands near the 140kt low end; EBITDA ~$1.05B at 6x plus a haircut for growth assets.

base.story: Copper ~$6-6.8/lb, 2027 copper ~150-160kt as guided, Snow Lake ~185koz gold, Copper World sanctioned late 2026/early 2027 with manageable capex inflation and Mitsubishi's last $180M by ~Jul 2027; EBITDA ~$1.55-1.6B and the stock tracks fair value plus a year of growth and cash build.

bull.story: Copper breaks to new highs ($7.5+/lb) on supply deficits; guidance delivered at the upper end; Copper World sanction plus Cactus PFS re-rate Hudbay as a US copper growth story; multiple expands to ~8-9x forward EBITDA on ~$1.9B.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$17 (-35%) the market cap (~$7.6B) is below 5x my 2027E EBITDA of $1.55B (~$7.75B) for the three operating mines alone, with nothing for Copper World (Mitsubishi's price implies ~$1.4B for Hudbay's 70%) or Cactus (~$1.1B paid in stock). Trading there would most likely mean a fundamental break: copper sustained below ~$5/lb, a Copper World capex/funding shock forcing equity issuance, a Copper Mountain ramp failure undercutting 2027 guidance, or a prolonged Constancia/Peru disruption, rather than ordinary 50-60% vol noise. It is above the $14.34 52-week low.

reasoning: HBM is Hudbay Minerals. On the reported 444.1M shares, $26.18 is a ~$11.6B market cap; with ~$20M attributable net debt (reported $80.5M net cash less Mitsubishi's 30% of $334.5M Copper World cash) EV is ~9.2x TTM EBITDA of $1.27B. Round 2 applies the supervisor's corrections. The Cactus base is $1,135.6M in shares, not US$1.48B (C$ headline), which cuts that SOTP leg by ~$0.3B. Shares are reported, not estimated. Copper World cash is now treated consistently. The 2027 volume step-up (+28%; 140-184kt vs 110-138kt) is confirmed, and Q3 consensus of $0.37 is higher than my own EPS build. So 2027E EBITDA goes from $1.45B to $1.55B, still below the 162kt midpoint for ramp risk, and EPS goes from $1.35 to $1.55 with the P/E cut from 20x to 17x. Net fair value moves from $25.0 to $25.6. I accept the supervisor's facts but land ~$1.4 below its $27: I haircut volume to ~155kt and hold a higher pre-sanction risk discount on Copper World and Cactus. I also do not credit the deck above spot. Lane work in round 2 focused, per the supervisor, on Hudbay-specific operating signals over generic sentiment. Corridor-blockade news shows no fresh Constancia disruption in 2026; the Sep 2025 shutdown remains the precedent risk. Snow Lake's Sep 28 plan (2043 life, 185koz/yr) is confirmed by trade press and the 6-K. Copper Mountain throughput is on plan per the MD&A; no independent alt-data was found. X/Reddit remain unreachable or empty, so research there is still limited. LunarCrush sentiment and the Simply Wall St CA$44.5 narrative are now excluded from any number. The Kalshi copper/gold settlements are kept as a metals read, but the thin Oct-30 book is not used. This round adds filings for basic reported facts, which the brief allows whatever the lane, so the in-lane share of sources is now below 60%. The 12-month distribution is a lognormal mixture (85% sigma 0.47, 15% sigma 0.80) with median ~$26.4, i.e. fair value plus a modest growth/cash-build drift; the scenario mean is ~$28.4 and P(>=26) ~0.51. The 1-month ladder centres at ~$26.3 with ~18.5% monthly vol and a fat-tail component for a likely in-window Q3 print.
